topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture aims
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture through its learning outcomes and the hallmarks framework used to explain cancer progression.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways allow cancer cells to sustain proliferation and survival despite normal growth controls.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation alters cancer cell maturity and tissue organization in hematological and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered p53 signaling and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins prevent cancer cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell proliferation and how increased telomerase expression lets tumors bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain p53's protective responses to cellular stress and consolidate how mutations undermine normal growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism characterizes cancer and can reinforce its development.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and vascular support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit a blood supply to sustain growth beyond the limits of oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and survival at secondary sites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the process of metastasis and the evidence for what enables disseminated cancer cells to establish secondary tumors.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's central aims, recommends further reading, and invites questions before the practicals.
